$comment: What each surface is made of, for the reflections and the specular response.
The usual trick for an old game -- match texture names like snow* or metal* -- cannot work here.
I.G.I.'s textures are NUMBERED: level 1 draws 203_04_1, 216_01_1_argb8888, 219_02_1 and a hundred
more like them, and no rule over those strings knows which one is glass.
So there are two ways to name a surface below.
*suffix        matches any texture ending that way. The one piece of meaning the names carry is
_argb8888, which marks the textures the packs store with an alpha channel -- in
this game the glass, the wire fences and the foliage.
exact_name     matches that one texture. Laborious, and the only honest way to say that a
particular numbered texture is polished metal: someone has to look at it.
An exact name beats a suffix rule. Roughness runs 0 (a mirror) to 1 (chalk); metallic is very
nearly always 0 or 1, because a surface is either a conductor or it is not.

default.$comment: Concrete, dirt, snow, painted metal -- the overwhelming majority of the game.

$comment: Glass, and the first surface in the game that reflects anything. It is also every wire fence
and every bush, which is the price of the only signal the names give -- a leaf reflecting the
sky is wrong, but it is a small wrongness on a surface that is mostly holes, and the Fresnel
term means it only shows at a grazing angle where a leaf is edge-on anyway.
Anything here that turns out to be foliage rather than glass should be listed by name below
with the default roughness put back.
$occlusion: Left out of the ambient occlusion, as occluder and as receiver. These are the cut-out
surfaces -- wire fences, foliage, glass -- and a depth buffer cannot describe them: it says
where a surface starts and never where it ends, so the horizon search treats a wire as a
solid slab reaching to infinity and darkens everything behind it.
